Hi! I've opened a small refactor PR #37749 extracting a lemma hf_modif_top from toStrongFEPair to match the pattern of hf_modif_int and hf_modif_FE.

It moves the hf_top proof into a standalone lemma and avoids duplication.

I'm currently working through the LSeries code for another project and came across this as a small cleanup.

Any feedback would be appreciated!
Thank you! I think similar simplifications like the one with simp you suggested can be made in other proofs in the file. I will look into it!

One question about your comment in this PR @Michael Rothgang ,

Is there a reason to prefer

simp [f_modif, mem_Ioi.mpr hx, notMem_Ioo_of_ge hx.le]

over

simp [f_modif, hx, hx.le]

which also seems to work?

I'm trying to get a better feel for when being more explicit is preferred over shorter simp arguments.
mem_Ioi and notMem_Ioo_of_ge are already simp lemmas --- so to me, the latter seems simpler. (This might be subjective.)

That makes sense, thanks!

As a follow-up: are PRs that mainly simplify things like this (e.g. removing explicit simp lemmas or replacing simp_rw blocks with shorter simp calls when possible) generally welcome, or do they just add noise?

For example, in f_modif_aux1 I was able to replace the longer simp_rw proof with a shorter simp using hypotheses like hx, hx'.le, etc. But maybe if this is like a self-contained file it's not worth it to keep simplifying it?
